InstrumentPhysical sciencesPreview

Spectrum Plot

A spectrum is a sampled measurement with uncertainty and a wavelength axis — not a decorative line. Keep the trace, its noise, the detected peaks, and the reference lines together, and make every number behind the picture inspectable.

Live

M42-SLIT-3 · M42 · slit 3 · UVES-like echelle (synthetic) · emission

Orion Nebula optical spectrum

Synthetic long-slit spectrum with Hβ, the [O III] doublet, Hα with its [N II] satellites, and the [S II] pair. The [S II] lines sit close to the 0.5 nm sampling limit.

441 points460–680 nm0.5 nm sampling5 peaksσ ≈ 1.552

Orion Nebula optical spectrum. 441 points from 460–680 nm. 5 peaks detected; strongest at 656 nm. 6 of 8 reference lines matched within 1 nm. Noise sigma is about 1.552 a.u.. 0 non-finite points ignored. Use the left and right arrow keys to inspect the spectrum, or open the data table for exact values.

RawSmoothed±1σPeaksReference

Hover or focus the chart, then use ← and → to inspect.

A synthetic optical spectrum of the Orion Nebula with Hβ, the [O III] doublet, Hα with its [N II] satellites, and the [S II] pair. Toggle raw and smoothed traces, remove a linear baseline, hide the peaks or reference lines, hover the chart or focus it and use the arrow keys, open the data table, or export the CSV.

What it checks

  • The raw trace stays available. Smoothing is a display and detection aid, not a replacement for the measurement. Switch back to raw at any time; the table keeps both columns.
  • Uncertainty is drawn, not implied. When points carry a one-sigma uncertainty, the chart draws a band around the working trace and the table reports each value. Points without an uncertainty are left as explicit gaps in the band.
  • Peaks have a definition. A peak needs a local extremum, a minimum prominence as a fraction of the observed range, and a minimum separation from stronger peaks. The table reports the wavelength, intensity, prominence, and FWHM.
  • Reference lines carry residuals. Each rest wavelength is matched to its nearest detected peak within the tolerance. The table shows observed minus rest, and marks a line as blended when more than one reference line shares the same peak.
  • Absorption looks for troughs. Set mode: "absorption" and the same detector finds minima instead of maxima. The axis, peak table, and export do not change shape.
  • Every sample is inspectable. The chart behaves as a slider over wavelength. Arrow keys, Home, and End move the cursor; the readout reports wavelength, intensity, uncertainty, and the nearest reference line.
  • The export is the data. CSV columns carry wavelength, raw intensity, smoothed intensity, baseline-corrected intensity, uncertainty, and a peak flag. The file does not contain the plotted screen coordinates.

How the analysis works

All three steps are deterministic and exported as pure helpers. They are display aids for review, not a substitute for a validated spectroscopic line-fitting workflow.

  • Smoothing. A centered moving average with an odd window (default 5 points), shrinking at the ends rather than padding.
  • Baseline. A straight line through the medians of the outer 10% of the trace. It removes a simple continuum tilt; it is not a physical continuum model.
  • Peaks. Local maxima with prominence of at least 4% of the observed range, separated by at least 1.5 wavelength units, capped at 24. FWHM is measured at half prominence by linear interpolation.
  • Matching. The nearest peak within 1.5 wavelength units (configurable). Residuals are reported in the same unit as the axis; a blended flag means the assignment is not unique.
  • Noise. A robust sigma from the median absolute first difference. It is a quick noise estimate, not a formal error propagation.

Data contract

  1. Data in. data is null or an object with an id, a name, and a non-empty points array. A missing or empty trace renders the empty state.
  2. Points are sorted, not trusted. Points are sorted by wavelength. A non-finite wavelength or intensity is dropped and counted in the header; a non-finite uncertainty is treated as missing, not as zero.
  3. Units are explicit. wavelengthUnit defaults to nm; intensityLabel defaults to Intensity and intensityUnit to a.u.. They appear on the axes, in the analysis, and in the CSV header.
  4. Reference lines are optional. Each line needs an id, a species, and a wavelength. An optional label adds a transition name. Without lines, the reference table is hidden and the rest of the instrument is unchanged.
  5. Analysis controls are options. smoothingWindow, minProminence, minSeparation, maxPeaks, and lineTolerance are passed once and shared by the chart, tables, summary, and export.
  6. Export is observable. onExport(csv) fires before the browser download. The component does not upload anything.
  7. Pure helpers are exported. summarizeSpectrum, smoothSpectrum, spectrumBaseline, findSpectrumPeaks, matchSpectrumLines, and spectrumCsv.

Accessibility

  • The chart exposes a slider role over wavelength. Arrow keys, Home, and End work without a pointer, and the value text names the nearest reference line when one matches.
  • A screen-reader summary states the point count, wavelength range, sampling, peak count, strongest peak, matched line count, noise sigma, and ignored non-finite points.
  • Peaks and reference matches are real tables with column headers and an explicit — for a missing value. The full data table is toggleable on screen and omitted from print unless opened.
  • Status is never color alone: peaks are labeled in the legend and the table, and the baseline, raw, and smoothed states are button labels with aria-pressed.
  • Layout uses logical properties and container queries. At 320 px the analysis moves below the chart without a page-level horizontal scroll.
  • There are no entrance animations or counting numbers. Reduced-motion users see the same chart immediately.

Preview status

The rendering, helpers, keyboard path, and export are complete and tested. The defaults still need a domain-advisor review: air versus vacuum wavelengths, the linear baseline, the smoothing and prominence thresholds, the line lists, and the absence of flux calibration or equivalent-width measurement. Treat this instrument as usable, not final. The Growth Curve and Dose–Response Curve carry the same preview status.
